title: Stadholder William III → Grand Pensionary Gaspar Fagel, letter in numerical cipher with Fagel's transcription (content printed; the key is the point)
correspondents: William III, Prince of Orange → Gaspar Fagel
shelfmark: Nationaal Archief, Den Haag, 3.01.18 (archief Gaspar Fagel), inv. 9, scan 10 (15 scans)
folio_note: Scan 10: numerical cipher, groups of 1-4 digits (e.g. '1460. 1614. 112. 172. 6. 102'), about 540 groups, signed by the prince and two other hands. The inventory says Fagel's transcription is folded in the letter. inv. 9 holds no other ciphered letter.
status: Existing for its content: a pencil note by an archivist on scan 0009 reads 'Gedrukt RGP 26 p. 314-316', i.e. Japikse, Correspondentie van Willem III en van Hans Willem Bentinck, 2e deel, I (RGP kleine serie 26, 1932). The three clear letters in the same file carry the same note (pp. 162, 184, 185). Only the cipher key may be new: a William III-Fagel numerical nomenclator, with Fagel's decipherment sheet, which could be rebuilt from this cipher/clear pair and applied to other William III <-> Fagel ciphers (e.g. the Royal House Archives, KHA). Related, also digitised and partly in cipher: 3.01.18 inv. 385-400 (Paets, Chieze, Heemskerck, Madrid 1672-86; same legation as battier1686) and inv. 346-370 (Wijngaerden, Van Haren, Wolfsen, Rumpf, Mortaigne; Denmark/Sweden 1672-87); inv. 370 (Mortaigne 1675-76) shows no cipher on a pass through its 42 scans. The States General copies in the catalogue (nos. 376, 377) are physical only.
why: A pair that gives the personal code of the stadholder and the pensionary during the Dutch War, a key for their other ciphers.
score_note: Scored from the NA inventory and a look at the scans, 4 Nov 2026 (research/dudout_leads_2026-11-04/, issue #254)
verify: Check that RGP 26 pp. 314-316 gives the whole ciphered text; align scan 10 with Fagel's transcription and the printed text to rebuild the key; look for other William III-Fagel ciphers (KHA).
prior_art: content printed: Japikse, RGP kleine serie 26 (1932), pp. 314-316 (archivist's note on scan 0009). Groen van Prinsterer, Archives de la maison d'Orange-Nassau, 2e série t. V, not checked. A published key not searched beyond this repo (catalogue.json, leads.json, targets/, 4 Nov 2026).

title: Cardinal Pascual de Aragón (Toledo) → his brother Pedro de Aragón, many letters partly or wholly in cipher, some with period decipherments
correspondents: Cardinal Pascual de Aragón <-> Pedro de Aragón; also the count of Medellín and Juan José de Austria
shelfmark: BNE Mss/2043 (olim G. 85), 682 ff.; BDH bdh0000042925
folio_note: Folios approximate (PDF page minus 2-4, read on a few leaves). f. 353 (read): 'Descifrado de las cartas de los numeros 31 a 84', a run of clear copies headed 'Carta del Cardenal mi S.r para el S.r D. Pedro...' (PDF pp. 0356-0373). Ciphered letters with the clear in the margin seen at about ff. 135-137, 482 and 498; the Inventario also lists ff. 459, 501, 590, 595, 636, 638 'descifradas al margen y a continuacion'. Wholly in cipher, no clear seen: about ff. 25-35, 50-53, 59-81, 214-233, and more. About 90-110 ciphered pieces, counted on thumbnails (plus or minus 20 %).
status: From the printed BNE Inventario general (not in the Europeana/BDH notices of the earlier sweep). Views checked on thumbnails and a few close-ups, 4 Nov 2026. The 'Descifrado 31-84' is a period decipherment: clear copies of about 50 letters, not yet paired with the ciphered letters. The ciphered letters seen all use one system: a mixed syllabic cipher of 1-2 digit numbers, letter- and syllable-signs and a few 3-digit codes. Our key from two marginal pairs did not validate (0.70 against a 0.85 threshold; shuffled-key control 0.46), so no reading is claimed. The Inventario's f. 34 note on 'el n.o 121 en la cifra del conde de Medellin' points to other keys; not found in close-up.
why: The cardinal's letters to his brother in the years of Valenzuela and Juan José's coup (1675-77), with period decipherments that can give the key for the many letters left in cipher.
score_note: Scored from the Inventario general and a thumbnail pass with a few close-ups, 4 Nov 2026 (research/dudout_leads_2026-11-04/, issue #254)
verify: Pair the 'Descifrado 31-84' copies with the ciphered letters they translate; rebuild the key from those pairs; then read the letters with no clear.

title: Count of Monterrey, the Constable of Castile and Francisco de Borja → the Duke of Villahermosa: letters in four ciphers, several with period translations
correspondents: Count of Monterrey; Constable of Castile; Francisco de Borja → Duke of Villahermosa (governor of the Spanish Netherlands from 1675)
folio_note: Folios approximate unless read. Pairs with a period clear in vol. 1 (Mss/2408): Monterrey, Brussels 30 Mar 1674, ff. 190-191v and a second ciphered copy, with 'Copia de carta de S.E. ... [desci]frada por el Duque, Brujas a 1.o de abril 1674' (ff. 192-193v, read); Monterrey, Brussels 8 Apr 1674 (clear f. 249, read) and 14 Apr 1674 ('Copia de carta ...'); Monterrey, Aranjuez 8 May 1675, clear in the margin (f. 139v); Constable, Madrid 11 Sep 1675, separate translation (f. 118, read). Borja, Madrid 1679 (both vols.): marginal glosses on part of the blocks only (about 15-30 % of the cipher). Ciphered with no clear seen: Monterrey 1674 (about ff. 175-177, 247-248, 260-263, 273-288, 330-338), Constable (vol. 1 f. 50; vol. 2 ff. 66, 79, 100-101, 107, 113-114 and two long runs), Monterrey 1675 (ff. 147-149), Borja 20 Dec 1673 (vol. 2 ff. 1-3) and 1679 (vol. 1 ff. 375-377). Group counts are rough visual estimates.
status: From the printed BNE Inventario general. Views checked on thumbnails and close-ups, 4 Nov 2026. The pairs listed in folio_note are period decipherments or translations (existing). Four systems, none of them the one of Mss/2043: Monterrey, Brussels 1674 (numbers 1-3 digits with isolated letter-signs, struck-through numbers probably nulls); Constable, Madrid 1673-75 (1-2 digit numbers with vowel-consonant digraphs); Monterrey, Madrid/Aranjuez 1675 (numbers with written syllables); Borja, Madrid 1673 and 1679 (dotted numbers with a nomenclator in thousands). The Inventario's 'Monterrey 1674 (siege of Oudenaarde) con su traduccion', 'Borja 18 Apr 1679 con su traduccion' and 'Constable 25 Oct 1673 con su traduccion' were not found as such. Rough extent left in cipher with no clear seen: 5,000-7,000 groups (Monterrey 1674), 3,000-4,000 (Constable), about 700 (Monterrey 1675), about 1,300 (Borja). No key built yet.
why: The Madrid court and the governor in Brussels writing in cipher during the Dutch War (1673-79); the period translations can give four keys for the letters left unread.
score_note: Scored from the Inventario general and a thumbnail pass with close-ups, 4 Nov 2026 (research/dudout_leads_2026-11-04/, issue #254)
verify: Rebuild the Monterrey 1674 key from the 30 Mar 1674 pair (two ciphered copies of the same text) and test it on 8 and 14 Apr; then the Constable key from 11 Sep 1675; read the letters with no clear.

title: William Harborne (Constantinople) → Walsingham, letters marked 'undeciphered', with deciphered siblings and a key probably preserved
shelfmark: TNA SP 97/1 ff. 54, 56, 58, 62, 66, 75 (Discovery C6766266-C6766275); candidate key SP 106/1 f. 3 (or f. 34)
folio_note: Long letters, e.g. 28 Jun 1584 (21 pp.) and 15 Sep 1584 (33 pp.), per CSP Foreign Eliz. ff. 36, 48, 68, 97 and 113 of the same volume carry period decipherments: a check set.
status: CSP Foreign Eliz. marks these letters 'undeciphered', while other pieces of the same volume carry period decipherments. Conyers Read (Mr Secretary Walsingham, 1925, III, p. 329) says the code was later used with Barton and that its key is in 'P.R.O. Cipher Book, Eliz. i, f. 3' (= SP 106/1); a note there gives f. 34. Barton's SP 97/2 has at least 13 pieces 'and decipher' (1590-92). Not seen by us.
why: The first English embassy to the Ottoman court, reported in cipher to Walsingham in the years before the Armada; this would replace lead 1254, whose letters are printed.
score_note: Scored from TNA Discovery, the Calendar of State Papers Foreign and Read (1925), 4 Nov 2026 (research/dudout_leads_2026-11-04/, issue #254); not viewed
